question: In view of plans to boost the budget of the military mobility programme to EUR 17.5 billion – more than a tenfold increase – and the role that Poland can play as a key transit and frontline country for the European Union, I have some questions about the practical implementation of the support scheme concerned. Poland has thus far completed 14 projects worth a total of EUR 222 million.

Those include significant increases in transport and logistics capacities at ports and airports. In the new financial planning period, investments in the Red Road (Gdynia), access to the terminal in Świnoujście and the modernisation of national road 16 (DK 16) may be of particular importance. With the above in mind: 1.
Have the proposed corridors already been precisely defined, or is their final shape still at the planning phase?
Does the Commission plan to give preferential treatment to frontline countries such as Poland, given their crucial importance for the security of the EU?
Does the Commission plan to make access to the military mobility programme budget conditional on compliance with the so-called rule-of-law criteria, as was the case with the Recovery Fund?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.2.2026) 1. The Council adopted the priority military mobility corridors in Annex II of the ‘Military Requirements for Military Mobility within and beyond the EU’ on 18 March 2025. The corridors serve to guide and prioritise future investments in the military mobility network at both EU and national levels.

In parallel, the Commission in cooperation with the Member States and the High Representative is working on identifying 500 ‘hotspot projects’ for urgent intervention on the corridors. 2. Ensuring smooth military mobility across Europe and across all four military mobility corridors is as important for the frontline countries, including Poland, as for the other Member States along the strategic military routes.

Nevertheless, as indicated in the Joint Communication1 accompanying the military mobility package, investments must be strategic, focusing on major choke points first and based on an assessment of the corridors’ functionality.

EU Financial support for dual-use infrastructure provided through the Connecting Europe Facility will primarily focus on supporting the four military mobility corridors across the Member States. 3. Respect for the rule of law remains a must for all EU funds. When implementing the EU budget, Member States and the Commission ensure compliance with the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights and respect of the EU values2.

Furthermore, under the general regime of conditionality3, the Commission is monitoring the situation in all Member States as regards breaches of rule of law principles with a sufficiently direct link to the EU budget.

September 2024 on the financial rules applicable to the general budget of the Union, https://commission.europa.eu/document/download/c2cfdb73-a86d-4c4c-b1cf-17ac9d052b0c_en. 3 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:32020R2092.
